title: pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticleReader
body:
## pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticleReader

Reads netCDF particle files of LODI, LLNL's Lagrangian atmospheric dispersion model: particle positions over time become a point mesh with per-particle quantities and, where defined, source groups as materials. Gridded LODI concentrations need pvVisItNetCDFLODIReader. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Positions are in the model's coordinate system; no geographic projection is applied.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays (materials in Materials): the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItNetCDFLODIParticleReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItNetCDFLODIParticleReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from LODI particle data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The LODI particle plugin offers per-particle quantities stored in the file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single LODI particle file to read (.nc, .cdf, .elev, .ncd); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The LODI particle plugin offers particle source identifiers (material set "sourceid") when the file defines them. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the LODI particle meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The LODI particle plugin reports a point mesh of particles named "particles". | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from LODI particle data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The LODI particle plugin offers per-particle quantities stored in the file; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticleReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
